title: Jeny's surprisingly stretchy cast-off
subtitle: A yarn-over cast-off for ribbing that stretches as freely as the knit fabric.
excerpt: Jeny's surprisingly stretchy cast-off works a reverse yarn over before each knit stitch and a forward yarn over before each purl, producing a cast-off chain as elastic as 1x1 or 2x2 ribbing.
sourceNotes: Published technique by Jeny Staiman. The yarn-over-in-pattern cast-off principle is based on established yarn-over cast-off mechanics documented in earlier twentieth-century British stitch literature, including Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938). This tutorial describes the method without reproducing the original text.

glossaryTerms.definition: A ribbing cast-off that works a reverse yarn over before each knit stitch and a forward yarn over before each purl, then passes the yarn over over the stitch. Produces an edge as elastic as the ribbing beneath.
A yarn over worked in the opposite direction from the standard: the yarn travels from back to front over the needle rather than front to back. Used in Jeny's cast-off before knit stitches.

content.text: adds a yarn over before each stitch, in the direction the rib pattern dictates, then passes that yarn over over the stitch as part of the cast-off. The edge stretches as freely as 1x1 or 2x2 ribbing. No standard cast-off can match it. The method is named for Jeny Staiman, who published it widely, though the yarn-over cast-off principle is older. Difficulty: intermediate, because you must decide the yarn-over direction before every stitch.
A ribbed piece (1x1 or 2x2) with live stitches
The rule: before every knit stitch, work a
(ryo). Before every purl stitch, work a standard forward yarn over (yo).
The first stitch is a knit: work a reverse yarn over (bring yarn from front, over the top of the right needle, to the back). Then knit the first stitch. Two loops on the right needle.
Pass the reverse yarn over over the knit stitch and off the right needle. One loop remains.
The next stitch is a purl: work a standard yarn over (bring yarn from back, over the top of the needle, to the front). Then purl the stitch. Two loops on the right needle.
Pass the yarn over over the purl stitch and off. One loop remains.
Pass the previous stitch over the current stitch (the standard cast-off motion). One loop remains.
Repeat steps 1-5 in pattern (ryo-k before each knit column; yo-p before each purl column) to the end of the row.

Sock patterns are the primary venue, because the sock cuff must stretch over the heel. It also suits hat brims and any neckline worked in ribbing. Whenever a pattern says 'cast off loosely in rib', Jeny's method is the most reliable way to achieve a truly elastic finish without going up many needle sizes.

items.symptom: Edge is no more elastic than a standard cast-off
items.cause: Using a standard yarn over before knit stitches instead of the reverse yarn over
items.fix: Check the direction: before a knit stitch, the yarn must travel over the needle from front to back (reverse). A standard yarn over before a knit creates a loop that does not add stretch.

items.symptom: Yarn overs and passes getting confused mid-row
items.cause: Losing track of the stitch pattern
items.fix: Look at the stitch about to be worked, not the one on the right needle, to decide which yarn-over direction to use. K stitches always get ryo; P stitches always get yo.
